summary: Potter County site; sources differ on the 1916 tower (steel Aermotor vs 20-ft wood), a 60-ft Aermotor was erected 1920, removed 1987; no tower stands today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1987 per register and Forest Lookouts; a hiking write-up says there is no longer a fire tower on the mountain

access.note: A gated forest road runs from East Cowley Road toward the summit; the sources read do not say who may pass the gate

visit.trail_note: Walk the gated Fox Mountain Tower Road from East Cowley Road, then take a 0.7-mile spur along the ridge to the summit clearing. Active logging was under way on the day of the described hike.

events.note: Register describes a steel Aermotor built 1916; Forest Lookouts lists a 20-foot wood tower built 1916
Forest Lookouts: a 60-foot Aermotor tower erected in 1920
Register: the Aermotor tower was removed in 1987; Forest Lookouts gives 1987 as removal without naming the tower
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on September 16, 2008

corrections.why: 6.1 m (20 ft) matches only the 20-foot wood tower Forest Lookouts lists for 1916. The same page lists a 60-foot (about 18.3 m) Aermotor erected in 1920. The sources disagree on which tower stood when, so the editor should confirm before changing the record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a steel Aermotor built in 1916. Forest Lookouts gives a 20-foot wood tower in 1916 and a 60-foot Aermotor erected in 1920. The sources are not reconciled; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The 1916 tower is described two ways (steel Aermotor in the register, 20-foot wood in Forest Lookouts), so facts.height_m uses the 60-foot Aermotor from 1920 and the correction is proposed, not applied. The MyHikes page is a trail-guide write-up, used only for the present-day condition and the route; it is not a survey. MyHikes lists ten photos but no URLs appear in the text read, so no photos were added. Elevation differs: the register gives 2,403 ft (732 m), MyHikes 2408 ft; elevation is not a fact key, so it is not used. No staffing or fire history in any source read; topic left out. The brief's coordinates match the register.
